text:
maya: heads up — we've been seeing a burst of internal svc call failures from GPU nodes in us-east-1 for the last ~20m. lots of 502/504s and a ton of DNS timeouts (500-3000ms).
jonathan: saw that. is this across zones or single AZ? any recent infra deploys?
maya: mostly az-3 and az-4, started right after a rolling kernel update window + a small RDMA driver rollout to a subset of GPU nodes. no app deploys around that time.
aditya: grabbing tcpdump from one affected node now. suspecting UDP issues — maybe fragmentation/reorder from RDMA offloads.
aditya: tcpdump snippet: ```
15:12:03.123456 IP 10.10.5.7.12345 > 10.10.0.2.53:  12345+ A? service.namespace.svc.cluster.local. (88)
15:12:03.123457 IP 10.10.0.2.53 > 10.10.5.7.12345: UDP, length 512
15:12:03.123458 IP 10.10.0.2.53 > 10.10.5.7.12345: UDP, length 1280 (truncated)
```
laura: that length > typical MTU — looks like responses are being fragmented. Are clients retrying over TCP? node-local-dns/iptables maybe blocking TCP fallback?
maya: interesting — pod-level kube-dns collisions maybe. node-local-dns is daemonset with iptables redirect to 127.0.0.53:53 on UDP only in our config. we intentionally disabled TCP to reduce NAT conntrack explosion.
aditya: that matches: dig +noall +answer @127.0.0.1 -p 53 big-svc... initially returns nothing, then on tcp attempt it works: ```
dig @127.0.0.1 -p 53 big-svc.namespace.svc.cluster.local +tcp +time=2
;; ANSWER SECTION:
big-svc.namespace.svc.cluster.local. 5 IN A 10.10.20.13
```
jonathan: so UDP truncated -> client needs TCP -> TCP blocked -> timeout. Why is UDP truncated though? MTU mismatch or offload causing reorder?
laura: two hypotheses: (1) RDMA/IB NIC offloads (GRO/GSO/LRO) + kernel bug producing reassembled segments bigger than path MTU, causing fragment drops mid-switch. (2) upstream CoreDNS answers have EDNS0 large response sizes (~4096) and intermediate infra doesn't support UDP fragmentation.
aditya: ran ethtool -k on igb0 of one bad node and saw GRO/GSO enabled. disabled them as a quick test: ```sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off lro off tso off``` after disabling, observed DNS latency drop from 800ms -> 30ms for the same queries.
maya: nice. any side effects of turning off offloads on GPU nodes (throughput)?
aditya: small CPU bump on network heavy benchmarks, but for our control-plane calls it's acceptable as a temporary mitigation. need longer-term fix.
laura: long term options: (a) allow TCP for node-local-dns -> safe but increases conntrack, (b) enforce EDNS0 size cap in CoreDNS upstream + enable truncation to force TCP-only for big answers, (c) fix NIC driver/firmware or RDMA config so segmentation honors MTU.
jonathan: for immediate rollback: can we flip a DaemonSet update to allow TCP on node-local-dns and bump conntrack on affected nodes?
maya: I can patch node-local-dns iptables redirect to include tcp and roll to az-3 only as a canary. also will open a firmware ticket with vendor for RDMA driver reports.
aditya: I'll schedule a zero-downtime toggle playbook: 1) patch ds to allow tcp/udp redirect, 2) increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on canary nodes, 3) watch DNS latency and conntrack counts via console.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0078 - node-local-dns UDP truncation spike impacting internal svc calls (linked: https://downtime.internal/INC-2026-0078)
laura: FYI for postmortem — add perf graphs: UDP truncated count, DNS TCP fallbacks, CPU impact when offloads disabled, RDMA firmware version per node.
maya: rolling canary now (az-3). i'll ping here when done and share metrics.
jonathan: thanks — also add a short-term alert rule: if dns_response_time_p50 > 400ms AND tcp_fallback_rate > 5% => paged to eng-infra.
aditya: can confirm canary nodes show 90% drop in DNS timeouts after allowing TCP. conntrack climbed ~4k but under new threshold.
maya: canary stable for 12m and no 502s. rolling az-4 next. will keep the RDMA/offload investigation running.
laura: good plan. assign postmortem to maya + aditya + network eng.
maya: assigned. closing thread once postmortem doc is linked here.
